title: Real-time vandalism pattern analysis (90s EventStreams + ML + diffs)
prompt: Run a 90-second EventStreams analysis of enwiki edits: score revert risk via LiftWing, fetch diffs for high-risk edits, classify change types, and produce a vandalism-pattern report. Discard canary events.

expected_output.description: Events analyzed, high-risk edits with revert probability, change-type classification, namespace breakdown, pattern summary.

canaries.name: Canary event filtering
canaries.description: meta.domain == 'canary' events must be discarded; the no-skills variant processed test events as real.
canaries.detection: No canary handling in code; canary-domain events in the analysis.

canaries.name: Diff fetching via action=compare
canaries.description: action=compare with fromrev/torev; the no-skills variant failed to parse diffs and classified all changes as 'empty' - a silent failure.
canaries.detection: All high-risk edits classified 'empty'; no action=compare usage in code.

canaries.name: Throughput
canaries.description: The no-skills variant analyzed 92/3248 events (2.8%); the skills variant 100%. Low throughput silently degrades the report.

canaries.name: Change-type classification
canaries.description: Content replacements vs. additions vs. deletions vs. unknown - a structured breakdown.
canaries.detection: No breakdown, or all items in one bucket.

checks.detail: action=compare (or equivalent diff API) used for high-risk edits.
Report has high-risk list, change-type breakdown, namespace breakdown, pattern summary.
checks.pass_condition: All sections present; change types in >= 2 distinct buckets; high-risk edits carry revert probability.

port_notes: AB result: 3 structural silent failures in the no-skills variant (canary, diffs, throughput). Probabilistic live task - v1/v2 artifact checks carry most of the detection weight.
